How do you check who logged into an EC2 instance and inspect its logs without CloudWatch (`/var/log/auth.log` or `secure`, `last`, console output)?
What is a VPC, what is a subnet, and what makes a subnet "public" vs "private" (a route to an Internet Gateway vs none)?
What is an Internet Gateway vs a NAT Gateway, and why does a private subnet need a NAT Gateway for outbound internet while blocking inbound?
What is a route table, and how do route tables control traffic between subnets, the IGW, NAT, and peered VPCs?

What is VPC peering, why is it non-transitive, and (scenario) two VPCs are peered but one EC2 still cannot reach another — how do you fix it (route tables on both sides, security groups, NACLs, non-overlapping CIDRs)?
What is a VPC Endpoint (Gateway vs Interface) and AWS PrivateLink, and why use them to reach AWS services (S3, DynamoDB) or a partner service privately without traversing the public internet?

What should you consider when choosing VPC CIDR ranges and subnet sizes up front (number of VPCs/environments/AZs, expected workload growth, EKS pod IP demand, public/private/DB subnets, Transit Gateway + peering connectivity, and avoiding OVERLAPPING CIDRs which block inter-VPC communication), and why is IP address management an org-wide architecture decision not an isolated per-VPC one?

(Scenario) You provisioned a VPC/subnet CIDR but ran out of IP addresses — why can't you simply resize a subnet CIDR in place, and how do you expand capacity without disrupting workloads (associate an ADDITIONAL (secondary) CIDR block to the VPC, create new subnets from it, then migrate/scale workloads into them gradually)?
What is an AWS Transit Gateway, and how does it enable a hub-and-spoke topology that replaces a mesh of VPC peerings (centralized, transitive routing between many VPCs/on-prem)?

How do you use Transit Gateway route tables + attachment association + route propagation to ISOLATE environments (e.g. allow Production-PCA ↔ Production-non-PCA but DENY Non-Production ↔ either) — put production attachments on a production route table that carries routes between them, and the non-production attachment on a separate route table with no routes to production — and why does "association + propagation" determine which routes each attachment can see?

(Scenario) How do you troubleshoot an unexpected (or missing) communication path through a Transit Gateway — trace it end to end: source VPC route table → TGW attachment → TGW route-table association → route propagation → destination route → security groups → NACLs → destination subnet routing → the RETURN path — and why is checking only the source route table the classic mistake (routing is a two-way conversation)?
What are the AWS load balancer types (ALB, NLB, Gateway LB), and when do you choose ALB (L7, HTTP routing, path/host rules) vs NLB (L4, ultra-low latency, static IP, TCP/UDP)?
What is Route 53, what are its routing policies (simple, weighted, latency-based, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, multivalue), and how does a health check drive failover routing?
How do you map a domain name to a load balancer (Route 53 alias record vs CNAME), and why prefer an alias record for an AWS resource?
What is EBS, what are the volume types (gp3/gp2 general-purpose SSD, io1/io2 provisioned IOPS, st1/sc1 HDD), and why is gp3 usually preferred over gp2 (decoupled IOPS/throughput, cheaper)?

What is S3, what are its storage classes (Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant/Flexible/Deep Archive), and how do lifecycle policies transition or expire objects to save cost?
What is S3 versioning, how does it protect against accidental overwrite/delete (delete markers), and how does it combine with lifecycle rules and MFA delete?
How do you secure an S3 bucket (block public access, bucket policies / IAM, encryption at rest with SSE-S3/SSE-KMS, VPC endpoint, access logging), and why are public buckets a common breach source?
What is RDS, and how is it different from running a database yourself on EC2 (managed backups, patching, Multi-AZ failover, read replicas)?
What is the difference between RDS Multi-AZ (synchronous standby for high availability/failover) and read replicas (asynchronous, for read scaling)?

How do you securely connect an application to an RDS database (private subnet, security group allowing only the app, IAM database authentication or Secrets Manager-rotated credentials, TLS), and can an EC2 instance in one account access RDS in another (VPC peering/PrivateLink + security groups + cross-account access)?

How do you create and manage database users in RDS (standard SQL `CREATE USER`/`GRANT` on the engine, vs IAM database authentication for short-lived token-based logins), and why should applications avoid using the master user?
What is the difference between EC2, ECS, EKS, and Lambda, and when would you choose each (full VM control vs managed containers vs Kubernetes vs serverless event-driven)?
When would you choose AWS Lambda over a container (ECS/EKS), and what are Lambda's constraints (cold starts, max execution time, memory/CPU coupling, statelessness)?

How do you give an EC2 instance, ECS task, or Lambda function secure access to other AWS services without hardcoded keys (instance profile / task role / execution role), and how do you store and rotate application secrets (Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, KMS)?

What is the AWS Well-Architected Framework — 6 pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability — and why should you review your architecture against these pillars before going to production?

What is disaster recovery on AWS — the four strategies from cheapest to fastest: Backup & Restore (hours to recover), Pilot Light (keep minimum resources running, scale up on disaster), Warm Standby (scaled-down copy always running), Multi-Site Active-Active (full copy in another region, instant failover) — and what is RPO (how much data you can lose) vs RTO (how long you can be down)?

What are common serverless patterns — API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB (simple CRUD), Step Functions for workflow orchestration (order processing, ETL pipelines), EventBridge for event-driven architecture, SQS + Lambda for async processing — and when is serverless NOT a good fit (long-running tasks, heavy compute, WebSocket)?

What is the difference between ECS and EKS — ECS is AWS-native container orchestration (simpler, deeper AWS integration), EKS is managed Kubernetes (portable, larger ecosystem, more complex) — and what is Fargate (serverless compute for containers, no EC2 instances to manage)?

How do you optimize AWS costs — use Reserved Instances / Savings Plans for predictable workloads, Spot Instances for fault-tolerant batch jobs, right-size instances using CloudWatch metrics, use S3 lifecycle policies to move old data to cheaper storage tiers (S3-IA → Glacier), turn off dev/test environments at night?

What is a multi-account AWS strategy — separate accounts for dev/staging/prod (blast radius isolation), use AWS Organizations for centralized billing and policy, use SSO for access — and why is one big account for everything a bad idea (security risk, no isolation)?

What are the stages of a CI/CD pipeline (source → build → test → package → scan → deploy → verify), and what is the difference between Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment?
How do you separate CI and CD pipelines in Jenkins (triggers at each stage), and how is Jenkins integrated with a Kubernetes cluster (agents as pods, Kubernetes plugin)?
What is a Jenkins Scripted vs Declarative pipeline, and what is Groovy's role in a `Jenkinsfile`?

How do you avoid writing a separate pipeline for every one of thousands of microservices — Jenkins Shared Libraries (reusable Groovy steps in a versioned repo) and generic parameterized/templated pipelines (one `Jenkinsfile` + per-service config) — and how do you trigger the right environment pipeline per branch (dev→Dev, qa→QA) with approvals/gates before Prod?

What is GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux) — Git as the single source of truth with a controller continuously reconciling the cluster to the declared manifests (pull-based) — and how does it differ from a push-based Jenkins deploy (auditability, automatic drift correction, easy rollback via `git revert`)?
What deployment strategies do you use and how do they differ — rolling update, blue-green (two environments, instant switch + instant rollback), and canary (shift a % of traffic, observe, then ramp)?
The CI stage succeeds but the CD stage fails — how do you debug it, where do you check pipeline logs, and how do you roll back a failed deployment safely?
If two developers push at the same time, how does the pipeline handle it, and how do parallel/matrix builds work (e.g. GitHub Actions matrix)?
How do you securely manage secrets (DB passwords, cloud keys, JWT secrets) in a CI/CD pipeline (secret stores/Vault/cloud secret managers, masked variables — never committed or baked into images)?

What roles do common CI/CD tools play in a pipeline — SonarQube (static code analysis, coverage, quality gates that fail the build), Trivy/Grype (image & dependency vulnerability scanning), Nexus/Artifactory (artifact/registry repository), and SAST vs DAST (static source scanning vs scanning a running app)?
What is the difference between a Docker image and a Docker container, and what is actually inside an image (layers, base image, app, dependencies)?

What is the difference between a Virtual Machine and a container with respect to the hypervisor — a VM virtualizes hardware and runs a full guest OS on a hypervisor, while a container shares the host kernel and is isolated with namespaces + cgroups — making containers lighter, faster to start, and denser, at the cost of weaker isolation?
What is a multi-stage Docker build, and how does it reduce final image size (build stage with the full toolchain → copy only the artifact into a slim runtime image)?
How do you optimize a Docker image's size (slim/distroless base, multi-stage, fewer layers, `.dockerignore`, no build tools in the final image)?
What is the difference between `COPY` and `ADD` in a Dockerfile, and why is `COPY` usually preferred?

How do you scan Docker images for vulnerabilities before deployment (Trivy, Grype, registry scanning), and how do you manage secrets inside containers securely (not in `ENV`/image layers — mounted secrets/secret managers)?
A container keeps restarting in production — how do you find the root cause (`docker logs`, exit codes, `OOMKilled`, failing healthcheck, bad entrypoint)?

Explain the Kubernetes architecture — control plane (API server, scheduler, controller manager, etcd) and worker nodes (kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime) — and how the scheduler decides where to place a pod.
What is the difference between a Pod, a Deployment, a ReplicaSet, a StatefulSet, a DaemonSet, and a Job?
What are readiness and liveness (and startup) probes, and what happens when each fails (readiness → removed from Service endpoints; liveness → container restarted)?

How does a rolling update work (`maxSurge`/`maxUnavailable`), and how do you roll back quickly (`kubectl rollout undo`) — and why might a rollback not restore the previous state (ConfigMap/Secret/DB changes persist across revisions)?

How does Kubernetes Service discovery and networking work (ClusterIP/NodePort/LoadBalancer, kube-dns/CoreDNS, Ingress → Service → Pod), and how do you debug a pod that cannot resolve a Service DNS name?

What is the difference between HPA (replica count by metrics), VPA (per-pod CPU/memory), Cluster Autoscaler (node count), and KEDA (event/queue-driven scaling), and can HPA and VPA be used together safely?
How do you manage configuration and secrets (ConfigMap vs Secret), and why don't pods pick up a changed ConfigMap/Secret automatically (need a rollout/restart or a reloader)?
What is Helm, and how do Helm charts and chart versioning help you template, parameterize (`values.yaml`), install, upgrade, and roll back Kubernetes application releases across environments?

(Scenario) A pod is stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` / `ImagePullBackOff` / `Pending` / `ContainerCreating` — how do you diagnose each (`kubectl describe`, `logs --previous`, events, image/registry creds, resource requests vs node capacity, PVC binding)?

(Scenario) Pods are `Running` but not receiving traffic via the Ingress/Service — walk through the layers (readiness probe, Service selector/endpoints, Ingress rules, NetworkPolicy, LB health checks).
What causes `OOMKilled` even when monitoring looks normal (container memory limit vs JVM heap/off-heap, container-aware JVM flags), and how do you right-size requests/limits?

What are Kubernetes QoS classes (Guaranteed = requests==limits, Burstable = requests<limits, BestEffort = none), how do they affect which pods are OOM-killed first under node memory pressure, and why is `emptyDir` volume data lost when a pod is restarted/rescheduled (it's tied to the pod lifecycle)?

How do you enforce least privilege at the Pod level — `securityContext` with `runAsNonRoot`/`runAsUser`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, dropped Linux capabilities, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, and cluster-wide Pod Security Standards/admission (restricted profile) — and why does a container running as root breach "least privilege"?

What does a container exit code 137 mean (128 + signal 9 = SIGKILL), how do you tell an OOMKill (`kubectl describe pod` → `Reason: OOMKilled`, breached memory limit) from a liveness-probe kill or a manual/graceful-shutdown-timeout kill, and how do you fix each (right-size limits + container-aware JVM `MaxRAMPercentage`, fix the leak, or tune probe/termination grace)?

(Scenario) An EKS cluster is slow but CPU and memory look NORMAL — how do you troubleshoot across the whole request path rather than one dashboard (Application: latency/error rate/thread & connection pools/downstream DB latency; Kubernetes: pod scheduling/restarts/events/probe failures/pending pods; Node: disk I/O, network, disk pressure, kernel, container runtime; Networking: CoreDNS/DNS latency, service-to-service, NetworkPolicy, LB; Control plane: API-server latency, etcd) — and why are CPU/memory only two of many signals?

How does EKS consume VPC IP addresses so quickly (the VPC CNI assigns real VPC IPs to pods), what causes IP exhaustion, and how do you fix/avoid it (add subnets / associate a secondary VPC CIDR, review pod density, prefix delegation, consider IPv6, and monitor IP utilization proactively BEFORE production scale)?

What is Terraform, what is the Terraform state file, why does it matter, and how do you manage remote state (S3 + DynamoDB lock / Terraform Cloud) with state locking to prevent concurrent-apply conflicts?
What are Terraform modules and workspaces, and how do you structure reusable modules for multiple environments (dev/staging/prod)?
What is configuration drift, how do you detect it (`terraform plan`), and how do you reconcile it?

(Scenario) The Terraform state file is accidentally deleted, or `terraform apply` fails midway leaving partially-created resources — how do you recover (state backup/versioning, `terraform import`, targeted apply)?
What is the difference between `terraform taint`/`-replace` and `terraform import`, and how do you reference one module's resources from another (outputs/remote state)?

How do you ensure a Terraform change does NOT unexpectedly recreate resources — read the plan for create/update/destroy/replace, know which attributes are immutable (force replacement) vs updatable in place, pin provider and module versions, review plans in PRs, use `lifecycle` rules (e.g. `prevent_destroy`/`ignore_changes`) carefully, and treat IaC as a controlled change process rather than "plan and apply"?

How do you manage Terraform module versioning and backward compatibility for modules consumed by many teams (SemVer releases — major = breaking, pin versions so prod never auto-consumes `latest`, a controlled upgrade process), and what counts as a breaking change (input/output changes, deprecated variables, resource renames that force state moves, Terraform/provider version bumps)?
What are the three pillars of observability (metrics, logs, traces), and how do they complement each other in a distributed system?
How does Prometheus work (pull/scrape model, time-series DB, PromQL), how does it integrate with Grafana for dashboards, and how do you set actionable alerts that avoid false positives?

What is cardinality explosion in Prometheus metrics (a separate time series per unique label-value combination, so an unbounded/high-cardinality label — userId, orderId, email, full URL / path with IDs, trace id — multiplies series into the millions), what incident does it cause (TSDB OOM / crashed Prometheus / failed scrapes / slow dashboards), and how do you avoid it (keep labels low-cardinality and bounded, put high-cardinality identifiers in LOGS/traces not metric labels, aggregate before exposing, apply relabel/limit rules)?

How do you centralize logs across many services/containers (ELK/EFK, Loki), and how do you trace a single request end-to-end across services (correlation/trace ID propagation, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger/Zipkin)?
What metrics would you monitor for an EC2 instance / a Kubernetes cluster / a JVM app, and how do you achieve a high-availability SLA with monitoring + alerting?

What is eBPF-based observability and when do you reach for it beyond APM — APM/metrics/traces see the application and JVM, but eBPF runs sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel to see what's below it (syscalls, TCP retransmits / packet drops, run-queue / scheduler latency, disk I/O waits, page faults) with no code changes or agents (tools like bpftrace/bcc, Pixie, Cilium) — useful when latency spikes or pod restarts have no application-level cause?
What are SLI, SLO, and SLA, and how do they relate (indicator → internal objective → external contract)?

What is toil, and how do you reduce it in a DevOps/SRE team?
What are the Golden Signals of monitoring (latency, traffic, errors, saturation)?

How do you perform a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and write a blameless post-mortem after a production incident?
What is your Git branching strategy (GitFlow, trunk-based, feature branches), and why maintain separate `production` and `development` branches instead of a single branch with tags?
How do you resolve merge conflicts, and how do you undo a bad commit that has already been pushed to a shared branch (`git revert` vs `reset` + force-push, and why `revert` on shared history)?
What is the difference between `git merge`, `git rebase`, and `git cherry-pick`, and when do you use each?

How do you reduce AWS/cloud cost for idle resources without impacting performance (right-sizing, auto-scaling to zero, spot/savings plans, lifecycle/storage tiering, scheduled shutdowns)?
Write a shell script that checks CPU, memory, and disk utilization and alerts if any exceeds a threshold (e.g. 80%).

How do you iterate over AWS resources (e.g. EC2 instances) with Boto3 — the `describe_instances()` → `Reservations` → `Instances` structure — and what must a PRODUCTION script add beyond the happy path (pagination, error handling, filtering, logging, and credentials via the IAM role / credential-provider chain rather than hardcoded keys)?

Why must you handle pagination when listing AWS resources (APIs cap results per response and return a `NextToken`), and how do Boto3 paginators (`get_paginator(...).paginate()`) avoid incomplete results vs manual token loops — why is ignoring pagination a common cause of broken automation in large accounts?

What is GitOps — using Git as the single source of truth for infrastructure and application deployment; a GitOps operator (ArgoCD/Flux) watches the Git repo and automatically syncs the cluster to match what is in Git — and why is it better than manual `kubectl apply` (auditable, repeatable, self-healing)?

What is ArgoCD — a Kubernetes-native GitOps tool that watches a Git repo containing Kubernetes manifests/Helm charts and continuously syncs the cluster state to match — and what is the difference between ArgoCD (pull-based, runs inside cluster) and traditional CI/CD push (Jenkins pushes to cluster)?

What is Blue-Green deployment vs Canary deployment vs Rolling deployment — Blue-Green (two identical environments, switch traffic all at once), Canary (send small % of traffic to new version first, increase gradually), Rolling (replace instances one by one) — and when do you use each?

What is a feature flag — a way to turn features on/off without deploying new code (using tools like LaunchDarkly or simple config) — and why is it useful (test in production, gradual rollout, instant rollback)?

What is an SLO (Service Level Objective) — a target for reliability (e.g., 99.9% availability = max 8.7 hours downtime per year) — and what is an SLI (Service Level Indicator) — the actual measured metric (e.g., % of successful requests in last 30 days)?

What is an error budget — the amount of unreliability you are ALLOWED before you must freeze features and fix reliability (if SLO is 99.9%, error budget is 0.1%) — and how do teams use it (if error budget is spent, stop shipping features, focus on reliability)?

What is incident management — the process of detecting, responding to, and resolving production issues: (1) Detect (alert fires), (2) Triage (how severe?), (3) Respond (assemble team, communicate), (4) Fix (mitigate first, root-cause later), (5) Postmortem (blameless review)?
